Leo’s class was going on a hilltop walk.

From the bus, the hill looked small and easy. A path curved through the trees, and blue marks showed the way.

“I will reach the top first,” Leo said.

Ms. Green smiled. “This is not a race. Stay with the group.”

Leo nodded, but he did not really listen.

At the start, everyone was happy. Birds chirped. Leaves moved in the wind.

Then Leo saw a tortoise near the path.

“Look!” said Amira. “A tortoise!”

Leo laughed. “Even I can beat him.”

The tortoise slowly moved one foot.

Then another.

Leo made a funny slow face, and everyone laughed.

After ten minutes, the path became steep.

After fifteen minutes, Leo’s legs felt tired.

“Water break,” said Ms. Green.

“Again?” Leo groaned. “We just started!”

Amira pointed to a rock. “Look, tiny shells!”

Ms. Green said, “Long ago, this hill was under water.”

The children gathered around.

Leo looked up at the hilltop. “I just want to reach there.”

When they began walking again, Leo rushed ahead.

He followed one blue mark. Then another.

Soon, he could not hear his class.

He came to two paths.

One had a blue mark. The other had a blue ribbon.

Leo chose the ribbon path.

Soon, his shoes sank into mud.

Squish!

He pulled one foot out.

His shoe stayed in the mud.

Leo hopped on one foot and shouted, “My shoe has become a mud sandwich!”

Amira and Ms. Green found him a minute later.

Everyone laughed, even Leo.

“The blue marks show our path,” Ms. Green said gently.

Leo cleaned his shoe and walked with the group.

This time, he slowed down.

He saw red ants carrying crumbs. He heard a bird that sounded like a whistle. He even saw the same tortoise moving slowly beside the path.

At last, they reached the top.

The view was beautiful. Trees spread below them like a green carpet.

Leo breathed deeply.

“We made it,” he said.

Amira grinned. “Even the tortoise?”

They looked back.

The tortoise was still far below.

Leo laughed. “Maybe he will reach tomorrow.”

On the way down, Ms. Green asked, “What did you enjoy most?”

Leo looked at the trees, the rocks, and his muddy shoe.

“The whole walk,” he said.

Then he added, “Except the mud sandwich.”
